title: Look up! Parallel Press’ Astro Black archives and protects the dazzling visual history of Black astronauts

paragraphs.text: Drawing on a cultural “fascination Black people have had with the planets and stars”, as well as the racial tensions surrounding the space race, this catalogue doesn’t just aim to pay homage to Black excellence in astrophysics, but to urgently protect Black history too.
paragraphs.translation: 借鑑了黑人對行星和恆星的文化「著迷」，以及圍繞太空競賽的種族緊張局勢，這本目錄不僅旨在向天體物理學領域的卓越黑人致敬，更在於緊急保護黑人歷史。

paragraphs.text: Astro Black is the first book to catalogue the stories of 18 Black astronauts. The stories of pilots, scientists and engineers who have shaped not just the face of space exploration, but also science itself – and therefore, design. When Parallel Press was created, one of its core goals was to organise and document Black accomplishment in every industry. Co-founders Akoua Smith and renald Louissaint, who had an incredible talk at June’s Nicer Tuesdays in New York City (soon to be on It’s Nice That’s YouTube), felt that there was not enough written about the extraordinary obstacles that Black professionals face in the US. For Akoua, these people weren’t just heroes, but fixations of her childhood, ever since her late father passed on a book about the Hubble Space Telescope. From there on, Akoua was shooting for the stars – and now they’ve been printed in this book.
paragraphs.translation: 《Astro Black》是第一本收錄了 18 位黑人太空人故事的書籍。這些故事記錄了飛行員、科學家和工程師，他們不僅塑造了太空探索的面貌，也影響了科學本身——進而影響了設計。當 Parallel Press 創立時，其核心目標之一便是整理並記錄各行各業中黑人的成就。共同創辦人 Akoua Smith 和 renald Louissaint（他們於六月在紐約市 Nicer Tuesdays 發表了精彩演講，該內容即將在 It’s Nice That 的 YouTube 頻道上線）認為，關於黑人專業人士在美國面臨的非凡障礙，相關記錄仍然不足。對 Akoua 而言，這些人不僅是英雄，更是她童年時期的執念，自從她已故的父親送給她一本關於哈伯太空望遠鏡的書後便是如此。從那時起，Akoua 便立志追求卓越（shooting for the stars）——而現在，這些「星星」已被印製在本書中。

paragraphs.text: To help trawling through Howard University’s Black Press Archive with materials sourced from the National Archives Catalog and the NASA Image & Video Library, the pair recruited an editor (as they do for every project), Taryn Finley, and they became a neat trio. The Black Press Archive became the foundation of the entire book, informing the sorts of experts they interviewed and cited throughout. The team found a doorway into new visual possibilities when they found that public domain imagery of space is stunning – but it was under threat. As the Trump administration brought more and more damage to federal programs such as the NASA image library, the team felt the urgency to print these images, to preserve history. You can’t delete a book. “Our goal is always to document Black achievement, so naturally, we wanted to make our first cultural index about our biggest feat yet,” says Akoua. “Looking up.”
paragraphs.translation: 為了協助搜尋霍華德大學黑人媒體檔案館，並結合來自國家檔案館目錄及 NASA 影像與影片庫的素材，這對搭檔招募了一位編輯 Taryn Finley（他們為每個項目都會這麼做），組成了精幹的三人組。黑人媒體檔案館成為整本書的基石，影響了他們採訪和引用的專家類型。當團隊發現公有領域的太空影像非常迷人時，他們發現了一扇通往全新視覺可能性的門——但這些影像正面臨威脅。隨著川普政府對 NASA 影像庫等聯邦計畫帶來日益嚴重的損害，團隊感到有必要印製這些圖像以保存歷史。你無法刪除一本書。Akoua 說：「我們的目標始終是記錄黑人的成就，因此很自然地，我們想讓我們的第一份文化索引圍繞著我們迄今為止最大的壯舉。抬頭仰望。」

paragraphs.translation: Parallel Press：《Astro Black》（版權所有 © Parallel Press, 2026）

paragraphs.text: Astro Black takes a lot of cues from space-age futurism and the dark colour schemes of space, but the book moves away from the flocculent galaxy-dust aesthetics we’ve seen for decades and instead shifts a focus to metallic textures, helping the book feel mechanical through images of boundary-pushing technology set against the black blanket of the solar system, massive rockets and rovers that remind us of how small we are. Thanks to Steven Horton Jr., friend of Parallel Press, the divider pages made use of a mesmerising monochromatic collage style that interprets constellations as ephemeral passages of time in space, making the process of flicking through the book feel like space travel itself.
paragraphs.translation: 《Astro Black》從太空時代未來主義和太空的深色調中汲取了大量靈感，但這本書擺脫了我們幾十年來常見的絮狀星系塵埃美學，轉而將焦點轉向金屬質感，透過與太陽系黑色背景、巨大火箭和探測車對比的前沿技術影像，讓這本書感覺極具機械感，提醒著我們人類是多麼渺小。感謝 Parallel Press 的朋友 Steven Horton Jr.，分隔頁使用了迷人的單色拼貼風格，將星座詮釋為太空中的短暫時光流逝，使翻閱這本書的過程感覺就像太空旅行本身。

paragraphs.text: “After two and a half years of research and development, we set out to have the content shine without any interference from the exterior, yet the white star on the soft matte black cover piques curiosity on a coffee table,” says Akoua. The page numbers float as the book moves forward. The indexes are rich with texture. The biographies are tactical and concise. The photography entrenches us in the confined world of Black human space travel and vast star-scapes.”
paragraphs.translation: Akoua 說：「經過兩年半的研究與開發，我們致力於讓內容本身閃耀而不受外觀干擾，然而柔軟啞光黑色封面上的一顆白星，在咖啡桌上卻能激起人們的好奇心。頁碼隨著書本的推進而漂浮。索引充滿了質感。傳記簡練而精確。攝影則讓我們沉浸在黑人人類太空旅行與浩瀚星空的受限世界中。」

paragraphs.text: The book also makes brilliant use of the media surrounding the space race, which included race politics. Around the same time, an explosion of blaxploitation films and urgent music surfaced to meet with the technological revolutions at the head of Western culture. “With Boris Gardiner’s Every N****r is a Star at the forefront of our minds, we chose to create our own symbol to represent the achievements of these 18 Black astronauts. For the title of the book, we reference the album Astro Black from Sun Ra’s Arkestra and the subsequent sample from producer Madlib’s album Quasimoto: The Unseen,” says renald. “We then turned to Gil Scott Heron’s poem Whitey on the Moon to help guide our tone. These references were integral to help ground ourselves in cultural history as we began to explore the wonder and fascination that Black people have had with the planets and the stars.”
paragraphs.translation: 這本書也出色地運用了太空競賽時期的相關媒體，其中包含種族政治。大約在同一時間，大量黑人剝削電影（blaxploitation films）和緊迫的音樂湧現，以應對西方文化尖端的技術革命。renald 說：「我們腦海中浮現著 Boris Gardiner 的《Every N****r is a Star》，選擇創造自己的符號來代表這 18 位黑人太空人的成就。書名則是參考了 Sun Ra 的 Arkestra 樂團專輯《Astro Black》，以及隨後製作人 Madlib 專輯《Quasimoto: The Unseen》中的取樣。」他接著說：「我們隨後轉向 Gil Scott Heron 的詩作《Whitey on the Moon》來引導我們的基調。當我們開始探索黑人對行星與恆星的奇想與著迷時，這些參考資料對於我們扎根於文化歷史至關重要。」

paragraphs.text: Paul M (He/Him) is a Junior Writer at It’s Nice That since May 2025. He studied (BA) Fine Art and has a strong interest in digital kitsch, multimedia painting, collage, nostalgia, analogue technology and all matters of strange stuff. pcm@itsnicethat.com
